title: Why Cooperation Is Not Simple: A Campus Lecture
instructions: 这是一份原创模拟教学材料（非官方雅思试题，也不对应任何官方分数）。请先听/读英文讲座，再完成10道题。听力部分包含说话人自然轮换与自我纠正，注意间接问句、名词性从句和比较/原因/假设表达。所有题目与选项均为英文；解释为中文。填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。
transcript:
NARRATOR: Welcome to this week's open lecture in the Hall Building. Our speaker is Dr. Lena Ortiz, a visiting lecturer in social science. The talk is called 'Why Cooperation Is Not Simple.'

DR. ORTIZ: Thank you. Before I start, let me correct one thing on the poster. It says I study 'teamwork.' I actually study cooperation — and those are not the same. Teamwork is one small part.

STUDENT (Maya): Sorry — can I ask what you mean at the beginning? Why do people say cooperation is simple?

DR. ORTIZ: Good question. Many textbooks suggest that cooperation is simple because people help when helping is cheap. I want to question that. I'll ask whether the cost is really the main reason, and what else might explain helping.

STUDENT (Maya): So you think cost is not important?

DR. ORTIZ: No — I think cost matters. I'm saying it is not the only thing that matters. Let me give an example from a simulated study. In one classroom game, students could share notes before a test. Sharing cost time. Some students shared anyway. Why? They said, 'I think my classmate will share with me later.' That belief — that others will respond — mattered more than the time cost.

STUDENT (Tom): Wait, is that a real study?

DR. ORTIZ: It's a simulated example for teaching, not a published finding. Please don't cite it as research. The point is the logic: if people expect a future return, they may help even when it is costly.

STUDENT (Tom): OK. So what would happen if nobody expected a return?

DR. ORTIZ: If no one expected a return, helping would probably drop — but not to zero. Some people help because they think it is the right thing to do. That reason is different from cost.

STUDENT (Maya): Can I check something? You said 'not to zero.' Do you mean some people always help?

DR. ORTIZ: I mean some people help in some situations, not always. That's an important difference. Now, compare two explanations. Explanation A says: people help when the cost is low. Explanation B says: people help when they expect a return or when they have a personal rule. Which is better? I think B explains more cases, but A is simpler. Simple is not always correct.

STUDENT (Tom): So which one should we use?

DR. ORTIZ: Use both, and ask what each one misses. That is the habit I want you to take away.

NARRATOR: That's all for today. The next lecture is on Friday at four.

grammar.title: 间接问句、名词性从句与比较/原因/假设表达
grammar.explanation: 本课先看意思：当我们要转述问题或想法时，常用一个从句来充当句子的一部分。比如“我想知道成本是不是主要原因”不是直接问句，而是把问句放进另一个句子里；这时问句内部用陈述语序（主语在前，动词在后），不用助动词倒装。名词性从句就是这样的从句，可以作主语、宾语或表语。比较表达用来对比两个解释；原因表达说明为什么；假设表达用if说明条件。注意：间接问句里不要用“do/does/did”倒装，也不要用问号。
grammar.example: I'll ask whether the cost is really the main reason, and what else might explain helping.

questions.evidence: I'll ask whether the cost is really the main reason, and what else might explain helping.

options: I wonder if the cost is important.
I wonder if is the cost important.
I wonder if does the cost important.
I wonder if important the cost is.
answers: I wonder if the cost is important.

questions.evidence: Explanation A says: people help when the cost is low.

answers: The reason why people help is that they expect a return.
